outcome: Complete blood count (WBC count, platelet count)
cohort: 200 neonates, including 100 born to mothers diagnosed with pregnancy-induced hypertension (study group) and 100 born to healthy mothers (control group).
finding: Neonates born to mothers with pregnancy-induced hypertension had significantly lower gestational age, birth weight, Apgar scores, mean WBC count, and mean platelet count, with a higher need for resuscitation, compared to neonates born to healthy mothers.
mod_finding: A significant difference in mode of delivery was observed, with 94% of mothers in the pregnancy-induced hypertension group delivering by cesarean section compared to 60% in the control group.
